rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Atoms, molecules, ions and radicals (valencies crossing into formulae) are counted by the mole (exact N_A = 6.02214076×10²³ since SI 2019) and weighed by amu (¹²C/12 ≈ 1.66×10⁻²⁷ kg). A_r is abundance-weighted (Cl 35.5); M_r is summed (H₂SO₄ 98, urea 60, CaCO₃ 100). The triangle n = m/M = V/22.4 = N/N_A (22.4 L at NEB STP: 0°C, 1 atm) interconverts everything.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: M_r is a pure number; molar mass carries g/mol — same digits, different quantities.  ·  22.4 L/mol needs all three: gas, 0°C, 1 atm (NEB STP).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 1 mole = 6.02214076×10²³ entities (Avogadro constant, Nₐ, exact since SI 2019). Molar mass (M) is g·mol⁻¹; for a compound M = Σ(atomic masses).  ·  n (mol) = mass/M = volume(ideal gas, STP)/22.4 L = N/Nₐ.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 50 kg urea sack holds countable moles only via N_A.  ·  '46-0-0' bag label is percentage composition compressed.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: basic concepts of chemistry: atoms, molecules, relative masses of atoms, molecules (within Foundation and Fundamentals).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.text: **Scope.** Basic concepts of chemistry: atoms, molecules, relative masses, amu, radicals, molecular and empirical formulae — Foundation and Fundamentals, Chemistry (class-11-notes).  ·  **Tested.** define it · list: basic concepts · one worked example · one misconception each.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Limiting reactant is the one consumed first; % yield = (experimental/theoretical)×100.  ·  M_r = 2 × vapour density (H₂ = 2 scale).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: SHORT (2 marks): Define amu and mole with their SI-2019 values.  ·  SHORT (2 marks): Compute M_r of urea and calcium carbonate.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: amu is a mass (kg), mole is a count — never interchange.  ·  Empirical gives ratio, never identity (CH₂O ×n family).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: amu = ¹²C/12; A_r weighted (Cl 35.5); M_r summed (H₂SO₄ 98).  ·  Mole exact N_A; triangle: n = m/M = V/22.4 = N/Nₐ.  ·  Empirical simplest ratio; molecular = n × empirical, n = M_r/E_r.  ·  Combustion analysis: C from CO₂ (×12/44), H from H₂O (×2/18), O by difference.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A_r is abundance-weighted average; Cl = 35.45 from 75.77% ³⁵Cl + 24.23% ³⁷Cl.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: SHORT (3 marks): 49 g H₂SO₄ → moles and molecules (show steps).  ·  SHORT (3 marks): Derive the empirical formula from 40% C, 6.7% H, 53.3% O data.  ·  SHORT (2 marks): Distinguish empirical from molecular formula with two examples.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: CaCO₃ kiln: 100 g → 56 g + 44 g as mole recipe.  ·  Glucose: CH₂O ×6 = C₆H₁₂O₆; lactic acid: CH₂O ×3 = C₃H₆O₃ (same ratio, different molecule).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: 1 amu equals → B  ·  Avogadro's number (SI 2019) is → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: # Basic concepts of chemistry: atoms, molecules, relative masses of atoms and molecules, atomic mass unit (amu), radicals, molecular formula, empirical formula ## 1. Topic Introduction Before chemistry can calculate anything — a fertilizer dose, a gas volume, a percentage — it must count particles it cannot see.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Conceptual Understanding ### What these concepts are - **Atom:** Smallest unit of an element retaining its chemical identity (H, O, Na). - **Molecule:** Two or more atoms bonded, acting as one unit — homoatomic (H₂, O₂, O₃) or heteroatomic (H₂O, CO₂, NH₃). - **Ion:** Charged atom or group (Na⁺, Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻).…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Explanation | Importance | |------|-------------------|-------------|-------------| | Atom | Smallest unit of an element retaining its chemical identity | Consists of nucleus (protons + neutrons) and electrons; defined by atomic number Z | Building block of all matter | | Molecule | Two or more atoms chemically bonded,…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: M_r = Σ A_r  ·  M_r = 2 × vapour density (H₂ = 2)  ·  % yield = (actual / theoretical) × 100

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: n = M_r / E_r (empirical → molecular)  ·  VD = 2 × M_r; limiting reactant = smallest (moles/coefficient).  ·  Ionic salts (NaCl) have empirical formulae only — no molecular formula.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Vapour density needs H₂ = 2 scale stated; M_r = 2×VD.  ·  Limiting reactant is not the smallest mass — it's smallest (moles/coefficient).  ·  % yield >100% means impure product or incomplete drying, not magic.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Chlorine A_r 35.5 = 0.7577×35 + 0.2423×37 (isotope weighted average).  ·  SHORT (2 marks): What is vapour density and how does it give M_r?  ·  SHORT (2 marks): Define limiting reactant and how to identify it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: SHORT (2 marks): Why does chlorine have A_r 35.5?  ·  LONG (5 marks): Explain the mole concept and interconvert mass, moles, particles and gas volume with examples.  ·  LONG (5 marks): Derive the molecular formula of glucose from composition data (M_r = 180).
